name: Saints John Fisher and Thomas More
history: A bishop and a layman who were put to death under Henry VIII for refusing to accept the king as head of the Church in England. John Fisher, bishop of Rochester, was beheaded on 22 June 1535; Thomas More, the former Lord Chancellor, on 6 July. Both were canonised in 1935. More is the patron of statesmen and politicians.
life: John Fisher was a Yorkshireman, a Cambridge scholar and chancellor of the university, confessor to Lady Margaret Beaufort and for thirty years bishop of the poor diocese of Rochester, which he refused to leave for richer sees. Thomas More was a London lawyer, a devoted father who educated his daughters as well as his son, the author of Utopia and a friend of Erasmus. He rose to be Lord Chancellor in 1529 and resigned in 1532. Both men held that the king’s first marriage was valid and that the Pope was head of the Church, and both refused the oath demanded by the Act of Succession in 1534. They were imprisoned in the Tower. While Fisher was there, Pope Paul III made him a cardinal. Fisher went to the block on Tower Hill on 22 June 1535, More on 6 July, declaring that he died the king’s good servant, but God’s first.
prayerTo: Saint John Fisher and Saint Thomas More, you served your king and your country faithfully, but you would not betray your conscience or the Church. Pray for all in public life, for lawyers and judges, for bishops, and for England. Give me a conscience formed by truth, and the courage and good humour to follow it. Amen.
penance: Pray today for those who govern, of every party, and for those who hold public office in your own area. More wore a hair shirt in secret; make a small hidden sacrifice for your country.
meditation: The king’s good servant, but God’s first. Where in your work do these two loyalties meet, and which comes first?
